title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): Grothendieck studies the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli multiplicities (orbifolds/stacks) M_{g,ν}. Y = D_0 is the compactified moduli space and Θ is the normal-crossings boundary divisor, with Y* = Y \ Θ. The boundary strata D' are normalized, so D' → Y is only a local immersion. It is étale onto the normalization of a closed stratum and need not be injective, because strata self-intersect. On p.69 he wants maps γ_{D'',D'} : π1 P_{D''*} → π1 P_{D'*} between fundamental groups of the 'punctured' neighbourhoods attached to nested strata D'' → D' → Y (diagram (234)). He stresses that γ comes from no actual morphism P_{D''*} → P_{D'*}. To construct it he introduces, independently of Θ, the 'tubular neighbourhood of D' in Y' as a germ of multiplicity containing D'.

This page explains the idea with pictures. If the image of D' in Y is a curve with a double point (a loop), the tubular neighbourhood drawn inside Y is a thickened band that overlaps itself at the double point. Drawn outside Y (abstractly), it is an unfolded U-shaped band containing D', mapping to Y by a local diffeomorphism. So V_{D',Y} is the germ along D' of a manifold W ⊃ D' together with an étale map (local diffeomorphism) W → Y extending D' → Y.

He then lists the settings where this works:
- For (pieces of) differentiable manifolds it exists as a germ of manifold around D', 'defined up to unique isomorphism'.
- For differentiable or even topological multiplicities (orbifolds/stacks) one can still define it as a germ, starting from a situation of pro-objects of manifolds (the germ seen as a pro-object of open neighbourhoods).
- The next page adds that one should be able to give a direct, more topological definition valid for any local immersion of topoi. It is denoted V_{D',Y}, it is functorial for composites D'' → D' → Y (diagram 2.35), and the deleted versions V*_{D',Y} are the inverse images of Y*.

The homotopy types (π1) of V*_{D',Y} are the local 'fundamental groups at infinity' attached to strata. This feeds the description of the Teichmüller groupoid near the boundary and its profinite Galois–Teichmüller analogue.
errors: Not an outright error, but a gap: 'defined up to unique isomorphism' holds for the germ of a local diffeomorphism extending D' → Y. This is fine when the germ is taken along D' with the étale map to Y as part of the data. For non-compact D' or wild immersions one needs care about Hausdorffness and the choice of neighbourhoods; the germ/pro-object formulation is what makes it work.
The topos-theoretic definition 'valable chaque fois [qu'on a] une immersion locale de topos' (next page) is only announced, with an explicit '(s.f. erreur)'. No construction or proof is given.

ideas.what: Tubular neighbourhood of a non-injective local immersion D' → Y, defined as the germ along D' of a manifold with an étale map to Y (it 'unfolds' the self-crossings of strata).
ideas.modern_name: tubular neighbourhood of an immersion / étale neighbourhood germ; for boundary strata of M_{g,n}: 'cusp neighbourhoods' or 'neighbourhoods at infinity' of normalized strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical differential topology (Whitney, Thom, Lang) for immersions; for M_{g,n} strata, implicit in Harer, Ivanov, Looijenga and Boggi
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses tubular neighbourhoods of boundary strata of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower informally; this explicit definition is not, to my knowledge, published.

ideas.what: Extension of the tubular-neighbourhood germ to differentiable or topological multiplicities (orbifolds/stacks) via pro-objects of manifolds.
ideas.modern_name: tubular neighbourhoods of sub-orbifolds / substacks; germs as pro-objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: Orbifold literature (Satake, Thurston, Moerdijk–Pronk); pro-object treatment of germs standard since SGA4

ideas.what: Proposed intrinsic definition of a tubular neighbourhood for any local immersion of topoi, functorial in composites D'' → D' → Y, with deleted version V* = preimage of the open complement.
ideas.modern_name: homotopy link / deleted tubular neighbourhood (Quinn's homotopy link; étale-homotopy analogues of punctured tubular neighbourhoods; Fujiwara/Gabber-type nearby-cycle neighbourhoods)
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); in algebraic geometry, nearby cycles (SGA7) and étale tubular neighbourhoods (e.g. Fujiwara, Friedlander)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a purely topos-theoretic 'tubular neighbourhood' V_{D',Y} attached to any local immersion of topoi. It would be functorial under composition and admit a deleted version over the open complement of a normal-crossings divisor, giving canonical 'specialization' maps between fundamental groups at infinity of nested strata. The general topos-level construction is not developed in the literature as such, though homotopy links and étale tubular neighbourhoods cover special cases.
missed.quote: Dans le cadre des multiplicités diff. (voire topologiques), on peut encore définir un voisinage comme un germe ... à partir d'une situation de variétés diff. (ou top.) pro-pointées[?]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A topos- or stack-level tubular neighbourhood with functoriality for nested strata would give a uniform framework for boundary specialization maps in Galois–Teichmüller theory. Examples are the tangential base points and the maps between inertia/fundamental groups of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} used by Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki and Boggi. It would also apply to stratified stacks generally. The ideas are, however, close to known constructions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a pictorial explanation of a classical notion: the tubular neighbourhood of an immersion, which unfolds self-intersections of boundary strata. The only somewhat original element is the suggested topos-level and orbifold generality with functoriality for nested strata, which is merely announced here. Related ideas exist (homotopy links, cusp neighbourhoods, étale tubular neighbourhoods).
transcription_corrections: 'et trace[?] en Y par' should most likely read 'et hors de Y par'. The contrast is between the band drawn inside Y (self-overlapping) and the abstract unfolded U-shaped band 'outside Y'.

Superscript over 'variétés différentiables': 'paramétrées[?]' is uncertain; it could be 'pures' or similar. 'prisms[?] (localement) de' is probably 'prises (localement) de' or 'pièces (localement) de', i.e. 'pieces of' manifolds.
'découlant[?]' in the inserted phrase probably stands for 'multiplicité' or 'découlant', replacing the struck-out 'topos'. The struck-out text reads 'germe de topos, par'.
'pro-pointées[?]' is uncertain; the reading could also be 'pro-...' something else (e.g. 'pro-représentées'). The intended sense is a pro-object of manifolds.
